# Badges

There are 114 badges to earn on the live map, plus 11 mishaps just for fun and 4 hidden badges that stay a secret until someone earns them. Tap any badge on the map to see your progress, how rare it is and who earned it first, or open the badges window from the 👤 menu.

Badges are worked out from your flights automatically. A few rules apply to all of them:

- **Visits:** an airport (and its country and continent) only counts when you land there having flown at least 50 nm, from an airport at least 30 nm away. Famous airports count from any distance, as long as you flew in from somewhere else.
- **Sped up, teleported or slewed** flights don't count towards landing, long-flight or visit badges.
- **Badge points** (the Badges leaderboard): 1 for a badge, 2 bronze, 4 silver, 8 gold, 5 for a special flight and 3 for a hidden badge. Mishaps are worth nothing.
- Special-flight landings at the difficult airports count at -175 fpm or gentler.

## Flying

- 🛫 **First flight** *(1 pt)*: Take off with the map watching.
- 🎫 **Frequent flyer** *(bronze, 2 pts)*: Fly 25 flights.
- 💯 **Century** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Fly 100 flights.
- 🏆 **Road warrior** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Fly 500 flights.
- ⏱️ **10 hours** *(1 pt)*: Fly 10 hours.
- 🕰️ **50 hours** *(bronze, 2 pts)*: Fly 50 hours.
- 🏅 **100 hours** *(1 pt)*: Fly 100 hours.
- ⌛ **250 hours** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Fly 250 hours.
- 👑 **1,000 hours** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Fly 1,000 hours.
- 📏 **10,000 miles** *(bronze, 2 pts)*: Fly 10,000 nm in total.
- 🔄 **Around the world** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Fly 21,600 nm in total (once round the Earth).
- 🛰️ **100,000 miles** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Fly 100,000 nm in total.
- 📅 **Regular** *(bronze, 2 pts)*: Fly on 7 days in a row.

  A day counts when you fly on it (UTC). Miss a day and the count starts again.
- 🗓️ **Dedicated** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Fly on 30 days in a row.
- 🔥 **Unstoppable** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Fly on 100 days in a row.
- 🏃 **Marathon day** *(1 pt)*: Fly 12 hours in one day (UTC).

## Places

- 📍 **Explorer** *(1 pt)*: Visit 10 different airports.

  An airport counts when you land there, flown in from another airport 50 nm or more away (or 50 nm or more flown from one at least 30 nm away). Circuits, hops between nearby airports and take-offs don't count.
- 🗺️ **Globetrotter** *(bronze, 2 pts)*: Visit 25 different airports.
- 🌐 **World tour** *(1 pt)*: Visit 50 different airports.
- 🧳 **Jet setter** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Visit 100 different airports.
- 🌏 **Been everywhere** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Visit 250 different airports.
- 📚 **Atlas** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Visit 500 different airports.
- 🛂 **Border hopper** *(bronze, 2 pts)*: Visit airports in 10 countries.

  A country counts when you land at one of its airports, flown in from another airport 50 nm or more away (or 50 nm or more flown from one at least 30 nm away).
- 📘 **Seen the world** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Visit airports in 25 countries.
- 🎌 **Citizen of the world** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Visit airports in 50 countries.
- 🧭 **Six continents** *(1 pt)*: Visit airports on 6 continents.

  A continent counts when you land at one of its airports, flown in from another airport 50 nm or more away (or 50 nm or more flown from one at least 30 nm away).
- ❄️ **All seven** *(1 pt)*: Visit airports on all 7 continents, Antarctica included.

  Antarctica has a few airfields, such as McMurdo's Phoenix Airfield (NZFX).
- 🌊 **Ocean crossing** *(1 pt)*: Fly across the Atlantic or Pacific.
- 🌗 **Equator crossing** *(1 pt)*: Fly from one hemisphere to the other.

  Take off in one hemisphere (north or south) and land in the other.
- ⏭️ **Date line** *(1 pt)*: Fly across the International Date Line.

  The International Date Line roughly follows 180° longitude, across the middle of the Pacific.
- 🧊 **Polar explorer** *(1 pt)*: Land north of the Arctic Circle or south of the Antarctic Circle.

  The Arctic Circle is at 66.56°N (and the Antarctic Circle at 66.56°S).
- ⛰️ **Mountain airport** *(1 pt)*: Land at an airport over 8,000 ft.

  The airport's elevation must be over 8,000 ft, such as La Paz, Cusco or Lhasa.
- 🌌 **Mountain by night** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Land in the dark at an airport over 8,000 ft.
- 🛥️ **Splashdown** *(1 pt)*: Land at a seaplane base.

## Destination of the week

- 🏙️ **Tourist** *(1 pt)*: Land at the destination of the week.

  Every week (Monday to Sunday, UTC) the map features a city or region. Land at any of its airports that week, flown in from an airport 50 nm or more away, for a passport stamp (circuits there don't count). It's not a race: everyone who visits gets one.
- 📸 **Sightseer** *(bronze, 2 pts)*: Collect 5 passport stamps.
- 🎒 **Seasoned traveller** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Collect 15 passport stamps.
- 🏛️ **Well travelled** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Collect 30 passport stamps.
- 🗓️ **Challenge accepted** *(1 pt)*: Finish all of a month's challenges.

  Finish every one of a month's challenges (your pilot page's Goals tab) before the month ends.
- 📆 **Month after month** *(bronze, 2 pts)*: Finish the monthly challenges 3 times.
- 🏆 **A year of challenges** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Finish the monthly challenges 12 times.
- 🧭 **Tour complete** *(1 pt)*: Fly every leg of a tour.

  Join a tour from your pilot page, then fly its legs in order, at your own pace.
- 🗺️ **Seasoned tourer** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Finish 5 tours.
- 🌍 **Grand tourer** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Finish 15 tours.

## Circuits

- 🔂 **Pattern work** *(bronze, 2 pts)*: Fly 10 circuits (take off and land at the same airport).

  A circuit is a flight that takes off and lands at the same airport: every touch-and-go counts, and so does landing, stopping and going round again.
- 🛞 **Circuit regular** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Fly 50 circuits.
- 🎖️ **Circuit master** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Fly 150 circuits.
- 🎓 **Circuit trainer** *(1 pt)*: Fly 5 circuits in one session (each within 10 minutes of the last).
- 📏 **Consistent** *(1 pt)*: Land 3 circuits in a row within 50 fpm of each other.

  Three circuits one after another, with all three landing rates within 50 fpm of each other (e.g. -120, -140 and -165 fpm). X-Plane landings have no rate yet, so they can't count.
- 🔁 **Round trip** *(1 pt)*: Fly out and back to the same airport on the same day (UTC).

  For example London to Paris and back to London, both on the same UTC day.
- 🎯 **Mission accomplished** *(1 pt)*: Fly a special mission with a filed route: pass every waypoint on it and land back where you took off.

  Plan a flight from and back to the same airport in SimBrief, with waypoints out there: each waypoint is an objective, ticked off when you pass within 2 nm of it.

## Aircraft and flights

- ✈️ **Type collector** *(bronze, 2 pts)*: Fly 5 different aircraft types.

  Each aircraft type counts once, by its ICAO code (A320 and A20N are two types; two A320 liveries are one).
- 🛩️ **Type rated** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Fly 10 different aircraft types.
- 🏗️ **Hangar full** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Fly 20 different aircraft types.
- 🔀 **Sim hopper** *(1 pt)*: Fly in 2 different simulators.

  Each simulator counts once: MSFS 2020, MSFS 2024, X-Plane and Prepar3D are all different.
- 🏕️ **Bush pilot** *(1 pt)*: Land away from any airport 5 times.

  Put it down where there's no airport: a field, a beach, a road or a lake. Seaplane bases count as airports, so a lake with one doesn't count.
- 🐋 **Heavy metal** *(1 pt)*: Fly a widebody.

  A widebody airliner such as a 747, 777, 787, A330, A350 or A380.
- 🚁 **Rotorhead** *(1 pt)*: Fly a helicopter.
- 🌀 **Whirlybird** *(1 pt)*: Fly a gyroplane (autogyro).

## Gliders

- 🪂 **Silent flight** *(1 pt)*: Fly a glider.
- 🦅 **Cross-country soaring** *(bronze, 2 pts)*: Fly 50 nm or more in a glider on one flight.
- ☀️ **Thermal hunter** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Fly 10 hours in gliders.

## Big aircraft, small airports

- 😬 **Shouldn't have** *(1 pt)*: Land a widebody (an A380, 747, 777…) at an airport whose longest runway is under 6,000 ft.

  A widebody (747, 777, A330 and the like) landing at an airport whose longest runway is under 6,000 ft. Each airport counts once.
- 🫣 **Tight squeeze** *(bronze, 2 pts)*: Land a widebody at 5 different airports with runways under 6,000 ft.
- 🙈 **Places I landed my A380 where I shouldn't have** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Land a widebody at 10 different airports with runways under 6,000 ft.

## Formation flying

- 🪽 **Formation** *(1 pt)*: Fly in formation: within 0.5 nm and 300 ft of another pilot for 10 minutes.

  Both of you in the air, within half a nautical mile and 300 ft of each other, for 10 minutes in a row. Fly with friends: a group flight is a good start, but you'll need to stay close.
- 🤝 **Wingman** *(bronze, 2 pts)*: Fly in formation on 10 flights.
- 🎪 **Display team** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Fly in formation on 50 flights.
- 🔗 **Tight formation** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Stay in formation for 60 minutes in a row.
- 🦆 **Big formation** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Fly in a formation of 4 or more pilots for 10 minutes.

  Four or more of you together, each close to the next (within half a mile and 300 ft), for 10 minutes in a row.

## Events

- 🎟️ **Event pilot** *(1 pt)*: Fly in an event.

  Fly in an event while it's on, from or to its airports.
- 🎫 **Regular attendee** *(bronze, 2 pts)*: Fly in 5 events.
- 🏟️ **Event veteran** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Fly in 25 events.
- ✅ **Made it** *(1 pt)*: Land at an event's arrival airport while it's on.
- 📣 **Host** *(1 pt)*: Fly the event you asked the UniFly Team for.

## Leaderboards

- 🥉 **Podium** *(1 pt)*: Finish a week in the top 3 for hours flown.

  Weeks run Monday to Sunday (UTC). Awarded when the week ends.
- 🥇 **Pilot of the week** *(1 pt)*: Finish a week 1st for hours flown.
- 🏆 **Pilot of the month** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Finish a calendar month 1st for hours flown.

  Months are calendar months (UTC). Crowned on the 1st for the month just gone, and shown on the leaderboards.
- 🏁 **Record holder** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Hold the fastest time on a route in your aircraft type (one flown there at least 3 times).

  Each route has a record for each aircraft type (so a 737 only races 737s, and Concorde other Concordes): the fastest whole flight, with no teleports or holding. See it on the route's page.

## Landings

- 🧈 **Butter** *(bronze, 2 pts)*: Land at -60 fpm or gentler.

  Measured at touchdown. Sped-up, teleported or slewed landings don't count.
- 🥐 **Butter chef** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Land at -60 fpm or gentler 10 times.
- 🏭 **Butter factory** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Land at -60 fpm or gentler 50 times.
- 🪶 **Feather** *(1 pt)*: Land at -30 fpm or gentler.
- 🎯 **Smooth operator** *(1 pt)*: Land at -100 fpm or gentler 5 times in a row.

  5 landings in a row, each at -100 fpm or gentler. A firmer landing starts the count again.
- 🧵 **Silk** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Land at -100 fpm or gentler 15 times in a row.
- 💋 **Kiss landing** *(silver, 4 pts)*: Land at -10 fpm or gentler.
- 🕛 **Midnight arrival** *(1 pt)*: Touch down within a minute of midnight (UTC).
- 📐 **Stable approach** *(1 pt)*: Descend steadily (300 to 1,300 fpm) and hold your speed (within 20 kts) all the way from 1,000 ft to 100 ft.

  Like a real airline stabilised approach: a steady descent and a steady speed (ground speed, so a big change in the wind on final can cost you it). The map has to see the whole final approach (it checks every second below 1,000 ft), so connect before you start your descent.
- 🌫️ **Low-vis landing** *(1 pt)*: Land when the airport's weather is IFR or worse.

  The airport's weather report (METAR) at the time you landed said IFR or LIFR: low cloud or poor visibility.
- 🌬️ **Crosswind** *(bronze, 2 pts)*: Land with a crosswind of 15 kt or more.

  Worked out from the airport's real-world weather report when you landed and the runway you landed on. The landing has to be measured at -600 fpm or gentler.
- 🌪️ **Crosswind master** *(gold, 8 pts)*: Land with a crosswind of 25 kt or more.
- 🍃 **Gusty** *(1 pt)*: Land in gusts of 30 kt or more.

  From the airport's real-world weather report when you landed. The landing has to be measured at -600 fpm or gentler.

## Special flights: famous routes

- 🌄 **Project Sunrise** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Fly Sydney to London or New York nonstop.

  Qantas's planned nonstop flights from Sydney to London and New York: around 20 hours and over 9,000 nm, the longest airline flights ever.
- 🦘 **Kangaroo route** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Fly Perth to London nonstop.

  The classic Australia to UK route, named in the 1940s. Qantas first flew it nonstop from Perth in 2018: about 17 hours.
- 🗽 **Singapore Sling** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Fly Singapore to New York nonstop, one of the longest flights in the world.

  Singapore Airlines' SQ23/24: around 18 hours and 8,300 nm, one of the longest scheduled flights in the world.
- 🐑 **World's shortest flight** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Fly Westray to Papa Westray (it takes about a minute).

  Loganair's 1.7-mile hop between two Orkney islands, the shortest scheduled flight in the world. It often takes under a minute.
- ⚡ **Supersonic** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Fly faster than Mach 1.

  Faster than the speed of sound, like Concorde. You'll need a fast jet (or Concorde) for this one.
- 🧲 **Over the top** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Fly within 5° of the North or South Pole.

  Pass north of 85°N or south of 85°S at some point in the flight. Some real Asia to America flights route over the Arctic.

## Special flights: difficult airports

- 🏔️ **Lukla** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Land at Lukla, Nepal (VNLK) at -175 fpm or gentler.

  Tenzing-Hillary Airport, the gateway to Everest: a 527 m runway on a 12% slope at 9,334 ft, with a mountain at one end and a drop at the other. There's no going around.
- 🐉 **Paro** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Land at Paro, Bhutan (VQPR) at -175 fpm or gentler.

  Bhutan's only international airport, in a deep valley between peaks of up to 18,000 ft. Only a handful of pilots are certified to land here; the approach weaves between the mountains.
- 🌺 **Madeira** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Land at Madeira (LPMA) at -175 fpm or gentler.

  Cristiano Ronaldo Airport: a runway partly built on columns above the sea, with strong, gusty winds off the mountains. One of Europe's toughest approaches.
- 🪨 **The Rock** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Land at Gibraltar (LXGB) at -175 fpm or gentler.

  Gibraltar's runway is crossed by the town's main road (the traffic stops for planes) and sits right below the Rock, which stirs up strong turbulence on approach.
- 🏖️ **Beach pass** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Land at Princess Juliana, St Maarten (TNCM) at -175 fpm or gentler.

  Princess Juliana: the famous approach over Maho Beach, where planes pass just above people on the sand before touching down.
- 🏝️ **Saba** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Land at Saba (TNCS), one of the shortest commercial runways, at -175 fpm or gentler.

  Saba's runway is about 400 m long, with cliffs dropping into the sea at both ends. Only short take-off aircraft like the Twin Otter fly in.
- ⛵ **St Barths** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Land at St Barthélemy (TFFJ) at -175 fpm or gentler.

  A short runway reached by a steep descent over a hilltop road, ending at a beach. Small aircraft only.
- ⛷️ **Altiport** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Land at Courchevel (LFLJ) at -175 fpm or gentler.

  A 537 m altiport in the French Alps with an 18.5% slope. You land uphill and take off downhill, with no second chances.
- 🚠 **Innsbruck** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Land at Innsbruck (LOWI) at -175 fpm or gentler.

  Tucked in a narrow Alpine valley with mountains all around; approaches follow the valley and need special training.
- 🎿 **Aspen** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Land at Aspen (KASE) at -175 fpm or gentler.

  A mountain airport at 7,800 ft in the Rockies, with a steep approach between peaks and often strong winds.
- 🥝 **Queenstown** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Land at Queenstown, New Zealand (NZQN) at -175 fpm or gentler.

  Surrounded by the Remarkables in New Zealand; approaches wind down the valley over Lake Wakatipu.
- 🏁 **Checkerboard** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Land at old Kai Tak, Hong Kong (VHHX) at -175 fpm or gentler.

  Hong Kong's old airport (closed 1998), famous for the low right turn over the city lined up on a checkerboard painted on a hill. Available as a sim add-on.
- 🐚 **Beach landing** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Land on the beach at Barra (EGPR) at -175 fpm or gentler.

  The only scheduled flights in the world that land on a beach (Traigh Mhòr, Outer Hebrides). The runways are marked with posts and covered by the sea at high tide.
- ☁️ **Roof of the world** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Land at Daocheng Yading (ZUDC), the highest airport, at -175 fpm or gentler.

  Daocheng Yading in China is the highest civil airport in the world, at 14,472 ft. The thin air makes for fast approaches.
- 🐻 **Svalbard** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Land at Longyearbyen, Svalbard (ENSB) at -175 fpm or gentler.

  Longyearbyen, at 78°N, is the northernmost airport with public flights, in the polar darkness for months of the year.
- 🐧 **End of the world** *(special flight, 5 pts)*: Land at Ushuaia (SAWH) at -175 fpm or gentler.

  Ushuaia in Argentina, the southernmost city in the world: approaches squeeze between the Andes and the Beagle Channel, often in strong winds.

## Mishaps 🙈

Just for fun, worth no points, and not counted in your badge total.

- 🧱 **Arrival by gravity**: Land harder than -600 fpm.
- 💥 **Lawn dart**: Land harder than -1,000 fpm, or hit the ground short of it. Ouch.
- 🚧 **Overrun**: Run off the end of the runway.
- 🌱 **The grass is greener**: Run off the side of the runway.
- 🐰 **Bunny hop**: Bounce a landing back into the air.
- 🛣️ **Taxiway special**: Touch down beside the runway (a taxiway, perhaps?).
- 🤷 **Close enough**: Land at the wrong airport, a few miles from where your plan was going.
- 🖥️ **Desktop crash**: Vanish from UniFly mid-flight and not come back.
- 💨 **Downwind dash**: Land with a tailwind of 10 kt or more.
- 🏎️ **Need for speed**: Taxi faster than 50 kts.
- 🎲 **Third time lucky**: Go around three times on one flight, then land.

## Hidden badges

There are 4 hidden badges. They aren't listed until you earn one, so you'll have to find them yourself.
